bull_case: Adobe absorbs model commoditization into distribution, file/workflow standards and enterprise integrations; AI ARR and MAU growth expand the ecosystem rather than bypass it.
bear_case: If agentic creation shifts outside Adobe workflows, application-layer switching costs can decay even while near-term ARR remains healthy.
thesis: The moat remains resilient at the workflow/ecosystem layer. Total ARR, RPO, MAU and AI-first ARR provide multiple scale observations, and Total Adobe ARR rises on a same-definition fiscal-year basis. That supports an 85 ecosystem score. However, direct switching-cost cases and market-share evidence remain incomplete, and AI model commoditization can still bypass application workflows; switching/pricing and commoditization resilience therefore remain at 75.

evidence.claim: Total Adobe ARR rose from the FY2026 beginning book of $25.66B to $27.50B at Q3.
Q3 RPO was $22.16B and Adobe reported >1B MAU across creativity and productivity.
Q3 AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650M and grew >150% y/y.
Creative freemium MAU crossed 100M and grew >70% y/y.

counterevidence: No same-definition market-share series or retention cohort proves that switching costs are strengthening.
Prompt-native and agentic tools can bypass Adobe applications and reduce application-layer lock-in.
Firefly-specific economics are not disclosed, so monetized AI usage does not by itself prove stronger moat economics.
unknowns: Same-definition creative workflow market share and retention over multiple years.
Whether agentic workflows reduce or deepen dependence on Adobe file/workflow standards.
falsifiers: Same-definition ARR contracts for multiple quarters while industry AI usage continues expanding.
Creative/Acrobat MAU grows but paid subscription revenue stagnates or declines.
Material enterprise workflows migrate away from Adobe file/integration standards.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Same-definition ARR growth, large RPO, expanding MAU and monetized AI adoption contradict persistent moat shrinkage as of the cutoff.

next_checks: Any disclosed retention or market-share trend for Creative/Acrobat.
Evidence that agentic workflows remain inside Adobe standards/integrations.

subscores.rationale: 75 strengthening anchor: recurring ARR and customer-group subscription growth remain strong; 90 structural strengthening is not supported by direct share/switching-cost evidence.
Observable anchor: 3+ verified ecosystem-scale figures (ARR, RPO, MAU, AI ARR) plus same-definition Total Adobe ARR growth are present; no concrete switching-cost case supports 90.
75 anchor: Adobe has multiple defense layers in distribution, workflows, files and model choice; evidence does not show that commoditization itself strengthens the moat, excluding 90.

uncertainties.rationale: ARR growth supports pricing/value, but direct switching-cost or share trend evidence is incomplete.
Multiple scale metrics and a same-definition ARR increase are observed; concrete switching-cost case is missing.
Adobe can integrate own and third-party models, but model-native workflows remain a credible bypass risk.
